deep.reconstruction:
Heading: 'Additamenta ad § 40 (Fundamenta nova, Jacobi)'. The page is a supplement to the q-expansions in §40 of Jacobi's Fundamenta Nova. Riemann says these formulas deserve study on the circle |q|=1, because there they yield functions of one real variable that are discontinuous at every argument value. Most of the series diverge for |q|=1. Integrating them term by term (with weight dq/q) gives series that do converge there. So he first lists the integrals of the base formulas 1–7: log k, log k', log 2K/π, 2K/π, 2kK/π, 2k'K/π and 2√k'K/π.

Modern dictionary: 2K/π = θ3², k = θ2²/θ3², k' = θ4²/θ3², 2kK/π = θ2², 2k'K/π = θ4², 2√k' K/π = θ3θ4 = θ4(q²)². Here θ3 = Σ q^{n²}, θ4(q) = θ3(−q) and θ2 = Σ_{a odd} q^{a²/4}.

The Lambert-series forms of the integrands are standard Jacobi formulas. I write them out myself and then integrate termwise.

(48) log(k/4√q) = 4Σ_n[log(1+q^{2n}) − log(1+q^{2n−1})] = −4Σ_{m≥1}(−1)^{m+1} q^m/(m(1+q^m)). Since ∫q^{m−1}dq/(1+q^m) = log(1+q^m)/m, we get ∫_0^q log(k/4√q) dq/q = −4Σ(−1)^{m+1} log(1+q^m)/m². That is −4lg(1+q) + (4/4)lg(1+q²) − (4/9)lg(1+q³) + …

(49) −log k' = 4Σ_n log((1+q^{2n−1})/(1−q^{2n−1})) = 8Σ_{m odd} q^m/(m(1−q^{2m})). Since ∫q^{m−1}dq/(1−q^{2m}) = (1/2m) log((1+q^m)/(1−q^m)), the integral is 4Σ_{m odd} m^{−2} log((1+q^m)/(1−q^m)).

(50) log(2K/π) = 4Σ_{m odd} q^m/(m(1+q^m)), so the integral is 4Σ_{m odd} log(1+q^m)/m².

(51) 2K/π − 1 has two Lambert forms:
- 4Σ_{m odd}(−1)^{(m−1)/2} q^m/(1−q^m). This gives −4Σ_{m odd}(−1)^{(m−1)/2} log(1−q^m)/m.
- 4Σ_{n≥1} q^n/(1+q^{2n}). This gives 4Σ arctan(q^n)/n. With arctan x = (i/2) log((1−ix)/(1+ix)), that is 2iΣ (1/n) log((1−iq^n)/(1+iq^n)).

(52) 2kK/π = θ2² has two forms:
- 4Σ_{m odd}(−1)^{(m−1)/2} q^{m/2}/(1−q^m). Termwise ∫ = (1/m) log((1+q^{m/2})/(1−q^{m/2})), giving 4lg((1+√q)/(1−√q)) − (4/3)lg(…√q³…) + …
- 4Σ_{m odd} q^{m/2}/(1+q^m). This gives 8Σ arctan(q^{m/2})/m = 4iΣ_{m odd}(1/m) log((1−i√q^m)/(1+i√q^m)).
This second form is the line whose label '53' and integrand Riemann struck out; the right-hand side is kept as a second expression for (52).

(53) 2k'K/π − 1 = θ3(−q)² − 1 has two forms:
- −4Σ_{m odd}(−1)^{(m−1)/2} q^m/(1+q^m). This gives −4lg(1+q) + (4/3)lg(1+q³) − …
- 4Σ(−1)^n q^n/(1+q^{2n}). This gives 2iΣ(−1)^n (1/n) log((1−iq^n)/(1+iq^n)).

(54) 2√k'K/π − 1 = θ4(q²)² − 1 has two forms:
- −4Σ_{m odd}(−1)^{(m−1)/2} q^{2m}/(1+q^{2m}). This gives −Σ(−1)^{(m−1)/2}(4/2m) log(1+q^{2m}).
- 4Σ(−1)^n q^{2n}/(1+q^{4n}). This gives 2iΣ(−1)^n (1/2n) log((1−iq^{2n})/(1+iq^{2n})).

In all cases the branch of the logarithm is chosen to vanish at q=0.

Next Riemann gives the same functions as power series, using Jacobi's notation (Fundamenta p.105).

(56) Expand 8Σ_{m odd}Σ_{j odd} q^{mj}/m. The coefficient of q^N (N odd) is 8σ(N)/N. Integrating gives 8Σ_{p odd} σ(p)p^{−2} q^p.

(57) Write N = 2^a p. The q^N coefficient of log(2K/π) is +4σ(p)/p if a=0 and −4σ(p)/p if a≥1. Dividing by N gives 4Σσ(p)p^{−2}(q^p − ½q^{2p} − ¼q^{4p} − …).

(55) For log(k/4√q), the coefficient of q^N is −4Σ_{m|N}(−1)^{m+N/m}/m. For a=0 this is −4σ(p)/p. For a≥1 the signs give σ(p)/p·[−1 + Σ_{b=1}^{a−1}2^{−b} − 2^{−a}] = −3σ(p)/(2^a p), so the coefficient is +12σ(p)/(2^a p). Dividing by N gives −4Σσ(p)p^{−2}(q^p − 3q^{2p}/4 − 3q^{4p}/16 − …).

(58)–(61) use Jacobi's expansion (§40, formulas 27–33). The expansion is θ3² = 1 + 4Σ_N (d1(N) − d3(N)) q^N, with d1, d3 the numbers of divisors ≡1, ≡3 mod 4. Here d1 − d3 is nonzero only for N = 2^λ s² n, where s is built from primes ≡3 (mod 4) and n is odd with all prime factors ≡1 (mod 4). In that case d1 − d3 = ψ(n), the number of divisors of n. Jacobi/Riemann write s² as (4m−1)².

(58) Integrating gives 4Σψ(n) q^{2^λ s² n}/(2^λ s² n).

(59) θ2² = 4Σ_{M odd}(d1−d3)(M) q^{M/2}, and q^{M/2} integrates to (2/M)q^{M/2}. This gives 8Σψ(n) q^{s²n/2}/(s²n).

(60) θ4² − 1 = 4Σ(−1)^N(d1−d3)(N)q^N. The odd N give the negative sum; the even N (exponent 2^{λ+1}s²n) give the positive sum.

(61) θ4(q²)² − 1 = 4Σ(−1)^N(d1−d3)(N)q^{2N}. Integrating gives 4Σ(−1)^N(d1−d3)(N) q^{2N}/(2N). The even-N part is 4Σψ(n)q^{2^{λ+2}s²n}/(2^{λ+2}s²n), as written. The odd-N part should be −2Σψ(n)q^{2s²n}/(s²n); Riemann wrote −4 (see errors).

Closing remark: these formulas can also be obtained by integrating Jacobi's formulas 27–33 of §40. The purpose of the whole page is to prepare boundary values at q = e^{ix}; the next page evaluates (48) at q = e^{ix} and treats rational x/2π.
errors: Formula 61, first sum: Riemann writes −4Σψ(n) q^{2(4m−1)²n}/((4m−1)²n). Integrating q^{2N} against dq/q gives q^{2N}/(2N), so the coefficient should be −2, or the denominator should be 2(4m−1)²n. Check: the q² term of ∫(θ4(q²)²−1)dq/q is −2q², consistent with −(4/2)lg(1+q²) in (54), not −4q². The second sum in (61) is correctly normalized (denominator 2^{λ+2}…).

Notational caveat in 58–61 (not strictly an error, inherited from Jacobi's notation): '(4m−1)²' must be read as the square of any odd number composed only of primes ≡3 mod 4, including 1. Taken literally with m≥1 it would omit s=1 and squares like 21²=441, which do occur.
In the second line of (54) the coefficient of the second term must be 2i/4. The image could be read as 4i/4; if so, that is a slip. The correct series is 2iΣ(−1)^n(1/2n)log((1−iq^{2n})/(1+iq^{2n})).
All other formulas, 48–60 including both representations in 51–54 and the divisor-sum forms 55–57, check out.

results.what: Termwise integrals ∫_0^q f dq/q of Jacobi's q-expansions of log k, log k', log(2K/π), 2K/π−1, 2kK/π, 2k'K/π−1 and 2√k'K/π−1, given as series of logarithms/arctangents (formulas 48–54).
results.modern_name: Integrated Lambert series for theta quotients (Eichler-type integrals of weight-1 theta series / logarithms of eta quotients)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Fragmente über die Grenzfälle der elliptischen Modulfunctionen (c.1852, published in Werke 1876 by Dedekind); base expansions Jacobi 1829

results.what: Power-series forms with divisor sums σ(p) for the integrals of log k, log k', log(2K/π) (55–57)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (Fundamenta Nova 1829) for the derivative forms; integrated forms in Riemann's Werke fragment

results.what: Integrated expansions 58–61 in terms of ψ(n) = number of divisors of n (primes ≡1 mod 4), derived from r2(N) = 4(d1−d3)(N)
results.modern_name: Integrated two-squares theta series (Jacobi's two-square theorem)
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi 1829 (two-squares formula); integrated form in Riemann's fragment

results.what: Programmatic idea: study the modular functions on the boundary |q|=1, where the integrated series converge and define everywhere-discontinuous functions of a real variable (leading to boundary values at q=e^{ix} and rational-point analysis on the next page)
results.modern_name: Boundary behaviour of modular forms / radial limits at cusps; precursor of Dedekind eta transformation and Dedekind sums

deep.surprise_reason: This is the opening page of Riemann's Latin fragment on the limiting cases of elliptic modular functions. The fragment was published in his Gesammelte Werke (1876) with Dedekind's commentary, and that commentary is the origin of Dedekind sums. The formulas themselves are termwise integrations of Jacobi's §40 expansions. The content is known and attributed to Riemann; only the small slip in (61) is a detail.

checkable.sympy: q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); lhs=integrate(series((t3**2-1)/q,q,0,30).removeO(),q); rhs=-4*sum((-1)**((m-1)//2)*log(1-q**m)/m for m in range(1,31,2)); simplify(series(lhs-rhs,q,0,30).removeO())==0

q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); lhs=integrate(series((t3**2-1)/q,q,0,30).removeO(),q); rhs=2*I*sum(log((1-I*q**n)/(1+I*q**n))/n for n in range(1,31)); simplify(expand(series(lhs-rhs,q,0,30).removeO()))==0

q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); A=sum(q**(n*(n+1)) for n in range(0,8)); f=series(log(A**2/t3**2),q,0,25).removeO(); lhs=integrate(expand(f/q),q); rhs=-4*sum((-1)**(m+1)*log(1+q**m)/m**2 for m in range(1,26)); simplify(series(lhs-rhs,q,0,25).removeO())==0

q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); t4=1+2*sum((-q)**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); f=series(-log(t4**2/t3**2),q,0,25).removeO(); lhs=integrate(expand(f/q),q); rhs=8*sum(divisor_sigma(p)*q**p/p**2 for p in range(1,25,2)); simplify(lhs-rhs)==0

q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); f=series(log(t3**2),q,0,33).removeO(); lhs=integrate(expand(f/q),q); rhs=4*sum(divisor_sigma(p)/p**2*(q**p-sum(q**(2**a*p)/2**a for a in range(1,6))) for p in range(1,33,2)); simplify(series(lhs-rhs,q,0,33).removeO())==0

q=symbols('q'); t3=1+2*sum(q**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); A=sum(q**(n*(n+1)) for n in range(0,8)); f=series(log(A**2/t3**2),q,0,33).removeO(); lhs=integrate(expand(f/q),q); rhs=-4*sum(divisor_sigma(p)/p**2*(q**p-sum(3*q**(2**a*p)/4**a for a in range(1,6))) for p in range(1,33,2)); simplify(series(lhs-rhs,q,0,33).removeO())==0
checkable.asserts: Formula 55: coefficients −4σ(p)/p² for q^p and +12σ(p)/(4^a p²) for q^{2^a p}

checkable.sympy: q=symbols('q'); t4=1+2*sum((-q)**(n**2) for n in range(1,8)); g=t4.subs(q,q**2)**2-1; lhs=integrate(expand(series(g/q,q,0,20).removeO()),q); lhs.coeff(q,2)
checkable.asserts: Formula 61 check: the q² coefficient of ∫(2√k'K/π−1)dq/q is −2 (Riemann's first sum gives −4, a slip)

checkable.sympy: N=45; (sum(1 for d in divisors(N) if d%4==1)-sum(1 for d in divisors(N) if d%4==3)) == len(divisors(5))
checkable.asserts: d1−d3 of N=2^λ s² n equals ψ(n)=number of divisors of n (here N=9·5)

transcription_corrections: In 52 the struck-out item is only the label '53.)' and its integrand; the right-hand side 4i lg((1−i√q)/(1+i√q)) + (4i/3)… is retained as a second representation of (52).
54, second line: the second coefficient should read 2i/4 (the transcription has this); the handwriting may look like 4i/4.
61, first sum: the transcription faithfully gives denominator (4m−1)²n, which is a slip in the original (should be 2(4m−1)²n or coefficient −2).
Heading: 'Additamenta ad §m. 40.' is Riemann's abbreviation for '§um 40'.
